stories.title: Persona 1 Remake Footage Seemingly Leaks Online
stories.summary: What appears to be gameplay footage from an unannounced Persona 1 remake has leaked online.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Persona 1 Remake Footage Seemingly Leaks Online
sources.text: What appears to be gameplay footage from an unannounced Persona 1 remake has leaked online. A little less than two minutes of video depicting what looks like a modern version of Sega and Atlus' original Persona game was first shared by a YouTube channel using the name P1REMAKE and was eventually picked up across social media platforms like Reddit . The YouTube account it's tied to was created in March 2010 and has seemingly posted just two other videos, with its previous upload published more than 14 years ago. The developers behind the RPG franchise have broached the topic of remakes for early installments in the past but never confirmed work was underway, meaning this could be our first look at the series' next remake. In the age of AI-generated fakes, you can never be too skeptical about things like this, but fans generally seem to be under the impression that the footage is authentic. While we won't share it here, you don't have to look too hard to see what everyone's talking about. Yea that Persona 1 remake leaked footage gotta be 100% real. I refuse to believe someone would do that much work to make a fake leak. There are a few reasons players suspect this to be our first glimpse at a not-so-secret Persona 1 remake from Atlus. Aside from the music, effects, and art, which all fall right in line with much of the studio's recent work, the video on display is much longer and more detailed than any fake leak would typically be. The smoking gun for many, though, is the character animations. It's specifically Eriko that people are calling out, as she seems to share a summoning animation with Persona 4 Revival 's version of Yukiko. Atlus' Persona 4 remake, of course, won't be out until February 18, 2027. There's also the issue of the appearance of Persona 2 protagonist Tatsuya, who seems to be standing in for what may be an unfinished character model. So, what can we make of all of this? Well, unfortunately, without confirmation from Sega or Atlus, not much. There is always the chance this could be an elaborate fake, with some of these odd details serving as evidence for that argument. On the other hand, it's possible placeholder assets and familiar animations are here specifically because the alleged Persona 1 remake is still very much in development. Persona 1 leak looks credible, not sure why people are reporting Tatsuya is replacing Masao, that's just complete bogus. This is most likely an internal investor pitch for remakes of Persona 1 and 2, and not actually Persona 1. There are Persona 4 Revival animations in the gameplay footage, which definitely helps the case of it being real. That sure is a persona 1 remake trailer. Why is tatsuya there We don't know when this footage would have been captured, even if it does turn out to be real. That means this could be from yesterday or years ago, with some speculating that the video we've seen today is little more than a proof-of-concept or pitch video. If the Persona: Be Your True Mind remake footage is authentic, it wouldn't be the biggest surprise to see it announced. Sega released its Persona 3 remake, Persona 3 Reload , in 2024, and will release Persona 4 Revival in just a few months. Atlus' P-Studio producer, Kazuhisa Wada, stopped short of confirming development for Persona 1 and 2 remakes in August of this year but still admitted that, as far as he's concerned, it's something "we have to do." Meanwhile, Atlus has absolutely suffered leaks before. The Persona 3 remake had in-development footage questioned by fans when it showed up online back in 2023. The upcoming Persona 6 , which, officially, we've seen little of so far, had images leak in June. A massive Steam leak in September then seemingly revealed a list of trophies – including story spoilers – for the upcoming installment. Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

sources.title: Rumor: Persona remake footage appears online
sources.text: A video reel showcasing what appears to be work-in-progress footage of a Revelations: Persona remake has surfaced online. The footage, a showreel similar to the one showcasing footage of Persona 3 Reload that leaked prior to its announcement, features three sections of the game—field, battle, and event scenes built around 2D illustrations. Persona 2: Innocent Sin protagonist Tatsuya Suou appears in the battle section of the footage. However, since he does not appear in Revelations: Persona , he may be a stand-in for another character. It’is also possible that remakes of Persona 2: Innocent Sin and / or Persona 2: Eternal Punishment are simultaneously in development. Other things worth noting are the constant appearance of Unreal Engine debut text in the upper-left corner of the screen and the fact that Eriko Kirishima appears to use the same Persona summon animation as Yukiko Amagi in Persona 4 Revival , lending the footage further credibility. As for the source of the footage, it was originally posted to YouTube by a user named “P1REMAKE” today at 2:25 a.m. PT / 5:25 a.m. ET . As of press time, the YouTube video remains accessible, but copies have also been hosted on file-sharing websites such as Gofile and Catbox , and shared in communities like r/GamingLeaksAndRumours . The YouTube account was created in March 2010 and has only ever posted two other videos, though its username was likely changed to “P1REMAKE” around the time the footage was posted.

sources.title: Two minutes of Persona 1 remake footage seemingly leaks online
sources.text: Two minutes of footage from an unannounced turn-based RPG recently spilled online, and yep, it very much looks like a remake of the very first Persona game. A YouTube account aptly called 'P1REMAKE' only yesterday posted a little under two minutes of footage from what appears to be a Persona 1 remake. As expected, eagle-eyed fans quickly spotted the clip and soon spread it across several other social media platforms, with the footage since appearing on Reddit and X. Of course, you should take all leaks with an unhealthily huge handful of salt no matter how convincing they look - especially in the age of generative-AI videos and such. At the same time, there are quite a few good reasons to let yourself be a little hopeful for this remake. For one, the two-minute clip is longer and more elaborate than gen-AI videos typically are. Several series fans have also pointed out the video shows Eriko summoning her Persona in combat, while using the exact same animation as Persona 4 Revival's version of bestie Yukiko. Revival doesn't actually launch until next year, which makes the pose quite suspicious. Then there's the fact that this type of leak isn't exactly new territory for Atlus' popular role-playing franchise. In 2023, footage from what ended up being called Persona 3 Reload leaked online and showed very similarly rough, clearly in-development scenes from the game's dungeons. One other curiosity is the inclusion of Tatsuya, the protagonist from Persona 2 Innocent Sin, who doesn't actually show up in the series' first game. Some folks are speculating that the video might have been created as an internal proof-of-concept pitch for Sega and Atlus management, so Tatsuya would serve as a placeholder model in that case. A Persona 1 remake isn't entirely unlikely with or without this potential leak, either. Persona series producer Kazuhisa Wada recently said remakes of the first two games are "probably eventually" happening at some point in the future. sources.title: Footage of a Persona 1 remake has seemingly leaked online
sources.text: Almost two minutes of footage from what appears to be a remake of the original Persona has leaked online. The clip, which seemingly gives the remake the subtitle Be Your True Mind, was shared on the GamingLeaksAndRumours subreddit . It was uploaded to file-sharing site Gofile on 31st October under a Japanese filename that translates as "Megami Ibunroku Persona Remake". Interestingly, the footage looks a lot like Atlus' more recent entries. It shows off stylish menus and a brief look at combat that closely resembles Persona 5 and Persona 3 Reload . There's also a short social link cutscene in a noticeably different, almost graphic novel art style. Fans digging through the clip believe they have spotted several details that lend it credibility. These include what looks like Unreal Engine debug text in the top left corner during battle (Atlus switched to Unreal Engine for Persona 3 Reload), a new remix of the original PlayStation game's Pandora theme, and the protagonist being referred to as "Boy With Earring", which is how he is named in Persona 2: Eternal Punishment . Atlus has not announced a Persona 1 remake, and we can't verify the footage, so treat all of this with the usual caveats. How do you solve a problem like Persona 4 ? stories.title: Xbox's Doom, Wolfenstein Developers Working 'More Closely Than Ever' Following Xbox 'Reset' Layoffs
stories.summary: Bethesda and Xbox development studio id Software, maker of the Doom franchise, has deepened its partnership with fellow Bethesda and Xbox studio MachineGames, makers of the most recent Wolfenstein games as well as 2024's Indiana Jones and the Great Circle.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Xbox's Doom, Wolfenstein Developers Working 'More Closely Than Ever' Following Xbox 'Reset' Layoffs
sources.text: Bethesda and Xbox development studio id Software, maker of the Doom franchise, has deepened its partnership with fellow Bethesda and Xbox studio MachineGames, makers of the most recent Wolfenstein games as well as 2024's Indiana Jones and the Great Circle. At a press event earlier this week for id Software's Doom: The Dark Ages - Revelations DLC, which was released this summer, studio co-director Marty Stratton was asked how the studio is doing in the wake of the layoffs that affected id as part of Xbox CEO Asha Sharma's ongoing Xbox " reset ." He answered, "We're doing great. Not to handwave the [layoffs] away...everybody knows we had about half of our studio exit as part of that. But there was a very deliberate effort to make sure that we were incredibly viable coming out of that across everything we do, across game development and technology department. "We're working more closely with MachineGames than ever. We've always had a very close partnership with them, but I think we're at a point with technology development that both teams are incredibly talented and have incredibly talented engineers and we're really on an amazing path that had started pre-[layoffs]. We'd kicked this off earlier this year. We're really excited about that. We're both really really bullish on what we have ahead." This is purely speculative on my part, but might the two decorated first-person shooter studios be co-developing MachineGames's next project, which is heavily rumored to be Wolfenstein 3 – with studio head Jerk Gustafsson saying, "We're not done with Wolfenstein yet"? Not only has MachineGames used id Software's idTech engine for every one of its games, but Sharma has publicly stated that she wants Xbox's development teams to double down on their biggest franchises – a sentiment echoed by Bethesda boss Jill Braff. And with id now seemingly done with Doom: The Dark Ages following the oustanding Revelations DLC, a team-up with MachineGames might help get the rumored third Wolfenstein game out the door faster, and getting games out more quickly is one of Sharma's goals. In addition, while Doom should certainly be considered in that "biggest franchises" group, Wolfenstein most likely is as well. Plus, Amazon has a Wolfenstein TV series in development, which might further incentivize Xbox and Bethesda to pair up id and MachineGames to make sure the latter team's next game is as awesome – and out as quickly – as possible. Bu whatever either team does next, the project(s) will be highly anticipated, at least by me, as both teams have incredible track records, both historically and recently. sources.title: id Software co-director says the Doom developer is 'working more closely with MachineGames than ever' after Xbox laid off 'about half of our studio'
sources.text: MachineGames is rumoured to be working on a third Wolfenstein game. Id Software has tightened its relationship with fellow shooter specialists MachineGames according to studio co-director Marty Stratton, after Xbox laid off roughly half of the Doom developer's employees earlier this year. Stratton was asked how the studio was doing following Xbox's massive job cuts at a recent press event for Doom: The Dark Ages' Revelations DLC (via IGN ) and he was keen to assure everyone that things are hunky dory at the legendary FPS developer. "We're doing great," Stratton explained. "Not to handwave the [layoffs] away … everybody knows we had about half of our studio exit as part of that. But there was a very deliberate effort to make sure that we were incredibly viable coming out of that across everything we do, across game development and [the] technology department." As part of its response to those layoffs, id Software has apparently deepened its ties with MachineGames, developers of Wolfenstein: The New Order and, more recently, the excellent Indiana Jones and the Great Circle . "We're working more closely with MachineGames than ever," Stratton said. "We've always had a very close partnership with them, but I think we're at the point with technology development that both teams are incredibly talented and have incredibly talented engineers and we're really on an amazing path that had started pre-[layoffs]. We'd kicked this off earlier this year. We're really excited about that. We're both really, really bullish on what we have ahead. Stratton's comments have led to speculation that the two developers may be cooperating on Wolfenstein 3, which MachineGames is rumoured to be working on . Id Software has just concluded active development of Doom: The Dark Ages following the expansions' release, so this is possible. What's interesting to me, however, is how Stratton repeatedly references technology. The id Software layoffs heavily impact the developer's Frankfurt arm, including numerous designers of the formidable id-tech engine. This led to fears that id-tech was being shelved. Microsoft contradicted this, though further reports left the question open . But Stratton's comments lead me to believe we might be seeing a tech alignment between the two developers as a result of those Frankfurt layoffs. While id Software built Doom: The Dark Ages on id-tech 8, MachineGames used a modified version of id-tech 7, called Motor, for Indiana Jones and the Great Circle. The fact that Stratton references both teams' "incredibly talented engineers" suggests to me that id Software is folding MachineGames' engine programmers directly into id-tech's ongoing development, with both teams working on the engine concurrently going forward. Assuming that id tech hasn't been canned outright, this approach would make sense given the expertise id Software lost from its Frankfurt arm. Sadly, the layoffs that affected id Software were far from the last at Xbox. After cutting 1600 jobs in the summer, Xbox initiated a second wave of layoffs in September that also saw Obsidian and Bethesda merge and put Activision in charge of Halo. sources.title: Final Fantasy 14 Evercold gets a four week delay - the MMO expansion now arrives in a busy February
sources.text: Pre-orders open on World of Warcraft: Forever's release date Final Fantasy 14 : Evercold has received a short and swift four-week delay. Square Enix 's MMORPG expansion was originally set to release in January of next year, but an update from Final Fantasy Fan Fest Japan has revealed that it's now due to come out during the packed month of February, 2027. Final Fantasy 14 boss Naoki Yoshida - affectionately dubbed Yoshi-P by fans - revealed the news during FF14 Fan Fest Japan. Evercold's new release date is officially February 23, 2027 with an early access period beginning on February 19, 2027. Of course, February is already packed with mammoth games - everything from Fable, God of War: Laufey, Persona 4 Revival, and Metro 2039 are seemingly taking shelter from GTA 6 . Here's hoping you have a spare few dozen hours a week for all the incoming goodies. Evercold pre-orders begin on November 4, which is funnily enough the official release date of Final Fantasy 14's biggest rival: World of Warcraft Forever. ( I'm sure it's just coincidental .) Pre-order bonuses include a Kottr minion that's part of the expansion's new, fluffy, feline race, as well as a pair of earrings and early access. You can check out all the different editions over on the official website - be warned, the Final Fantasy 13 mount might tempt you to put a dent in your wallet. sources.title: Fan-made Oblivion remake Skyblivion runs into legal trouble with a former volunteer
sources.text: "A 'take your ball and go home' approach like this fundamentally contradicts the collaborative, open spirit of the modding community" Skyblivion (the fan-made Oblivion remake that's being rebuilt inside of Skyrim) has been a long time coming, but we might need to wait a while longer for the conversion mod to see the light of day due to a new legal issue. One of the ambitious project's lead modders, Rebelzize, today uploaded a video about the ongoing situation. "Recently, a former volunteer who contributed to Skyblivion's development departed the project. We want to be completely transparent with the community about what has happened since their departure," he explains in the description. "After they left the project, we had several discussions regarding the continued use and maintenance of his work. The main disagreement centered on their objection to our decompilation of parts of their work — a necessary step our team took to maintain functionality and fix issues in systems already built into the project after access to the original source code repository was revoked," Rebelzize adds. Rebelzize doesn't name the former modder in an effort to avoid creating an online "witch hunt," but they eventually sent the Skyblivion folks a series of legal threats demanding the real names and home addresses of several other volunteer team members - "something that we are simply not willing to share with somebody that we don't even know," Rebelzize says, calling the demands "disproportionate." The former modder is apparently looking to sue for damages worth upwards of €30,000. "A 'take your ball and go home' approach like this fundamentally contradicts the collaborative, open spirit of the modding community that makes massive passion projects like this possible," Rebelzize continues. "To protect our volunteers from undue stress and ensure a clean break, in good faith we removed their code, rebuilding and improving the system from the ground up." Despite removing their work from Skyblivion, the anonymous former volunteer has apparently "continued to intensify their threats." The Skyblivion team is now looking for help from anyone experienced in IP and GDPR law, pointing interested folks toward their official website . Last year, it looked like a Skyblivion release date could be right around the corner . There's still no word on when we can expect the gorgeous fan-led revival, though. Known as “ Skyblivion ” the fan-project has spent over a decade in development. While a lengthy development is often filled with ups and downs, its latest woe is a rather unique one, as developers say that one of their former members is threatening litigation . “Recently, a former volunteer who contributed to Skyblivion âs development departed the project,” posted The Elder Scrolls Renewal Project . “We want to be completely transparent with the community about what has happened since their departure.” A former volunteer is attempting to sue Skyblivion and we need your help pic.twitter.com/3Ee5eQTELG — Skyblivion (@TESRSkyblivion) October 30, 2026 According to the statement, an unnamed volunteer contributor left the team a short time ago. Since leaving, there has been a great deal of contention around the work they left behind. The former developer, according to the post, objected to the “decompilation of parts of their work,” something bound to happen as other aspects are reworked and improved. In response, the disgruntled party sent a legal threat, demanding the real names of others involved. To temper the situation, the statement says they decided to remove the code and contributions in question, but despite that the former member has “continued to intensify their threats.” In a video plea , Kyle Rebel says that one anonymous community member demanding the legal names of the others is unacceptable. In kind, they also ask supporters not to”make this a witch-hunt,” requesting pro-bono legal assistance and resources over any online campaign to sniff out the unnamed troll. sources.title: Nintendo Reveals Surprise Pikmin Day Direct
sources.text: Nintendo has revealed a surprise Nintendo Direct for Pikmin Day because it has apparently decided that's a thing now. Instead of spooky game announcements or horror movie memes, video game fans woke up to on Halloween 2026 was Mario creator Shigeru Miyamoto's face. That's because Nintendo has declared November 1 as Pikmin Day, and it's got a brand-new Direct to celebrate the occasion. Yes, really. None of this is a joke. There's a little more than nine minutes of announcements to go over. Although there's no Pikmin 5 reveal or anything else too groundbreaking here, Miyamoto did take the time to share new information about Pikmin 4 and promised that, "going forward, I want people to know more about Pikmin." Tomorrow is Pikmin Day! Join in on the fun by playing Pikmin games on Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch. https://t.co/iYxZldya7p So, to start, why is the first of November Pikmin Day? Nintendo's miniaturized franchise launched in Japan in October 2001 before coming to North America in December, so there's no tie to a release date like you might have guessed. Instead, Miyamoto explained that November 1 is Pikmin Day because there were originally only three Pikmin, which, when standing next to each other, kinda looks like "11.1." Ready to test your skills at Dandori Academy? A free demo of #Pikmin4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy will be available on Nov 2. https://t.co/rNHNq35RMT You gotta give 'em credit for creativity, as Pikmin Day is probably one of the last things anyone expected to see today. Still, it served as a nice opportunity to offer an update on Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy ahead of its release November 12, 2026. Players will be able to use the new consoles built-in microphone to Oatchi, controlling them by using commands like 'rush' and 'go to work.' The Dandori Academy mode, meanwhile, comes with new challenges, including exams that take place on Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays, that give players timed tasks and an opportunity to earn medals. A demo for the Switch 2 version of Pikimin 4 will be available starting November 2, with save data available to transfer to the full launch. It offers access to the Sun-Speckled Terrace opening area, as well as two Dandori Academy stages. Secret Caves are coming this winter! Get ready to explore Secret Caves, face off against familiar creatures, and uncover hidden treasures along the way in @PikminBloom on your smartphone. https://t.co/Nx6Lzba6v4 Nintendo first brought its augmented-reality game, Pikmin Bloom, to smartphone devices in 2021, but five years on, and it's still got more to give. As shown in a teaser video featuring a group of the colorful plant-like creatures battling a Bulborb, an update scheduled to arrive this winter will add a new mechanic called Secret Caves. These battle-focused exploration events allow players to take their crew into caves to battle creatures and earn rewards. Before a cave is explored, players must collect a cave map, which feature information about a cave and can be found on things like Postcards. Then, Pikmin are sent into the cave to search for treasures, with some of the items highlighted during the Direct including a rubber duck, a sword, a cookie, and a chef hat. Should a battle ensue, you'll command your army by sending them in to attack when the moment is right, or retreat if things get too hairy. Pikmin 4's Dandori Academy challenges also give players an opportunity to collect maps by taking exams. If you couldn't tell from the video games, shorts , and Easter Eggs Nintendo has highlighted through the franchise's 25-year history, it's got a soft spot for Pikmin. Miyamoto has spearheaded this charge, and because he wants people to know more about the company's adorable little mascots, he's enlisted some help. Joining him during the Nintendo Direct broadcast was Japanese actress and crafty Pikmin fan Fuka Koshiba. Known for her work on TV projects like Siren and films like Lady Kaga, Miyamoto brought her in to help him "build more excitement around Pikmin going forward" after she shared hand-made Pikmin-themed hats on Instagram. "Originally, I had heard on social media that you could get hats of the Red Pikmin, Blue Pikmin, and Yellow Pikmin from those claw machines," Koshiba said, holding one of her hats. "I'm not good at the claw machines, but I really wanted the hats, so I thought, 'Well, let's just knit them.'" "I see," Miyamoto replied. "I'm also bad at the claw machines." That was a close one! Watch Hello! Pikmin short movies and enjoy new Pikmin adventures. https://t.co/8OPB48hDZr The Pikmin Day Direct also featured a brand-new Pikmin Original Short Movie. Following last year's Close to You short, this video sees a Red Pikmin do its best to grab a baseball from a frog. It's as cute as you could ever expect. As part of Nintendo's initiative to lean harder into the series, new shorts will be released monthly via the Nintendo Today! app, as well as other channels. However, there will also be a new episode released tomorrow, with another set to follow sometime in November. Miyamoto said he's collaborating with Nintendo Pictures staff to make the shorts. That's all for the Pikmin Day Direct. While there was no hint at anything like Pikmin 5, planting November 1 as an official holiday is probably a sign that Nintendo has no intention of putting a cap on Pikmin content anytime soon. While we wait for any bigger updates on the franchise, you can check out IGN's 9/10 Pikmin 4 review . Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. sources.text: Funcom will also "continue expanding the game" through 2027. Thus far, Funcom has focussed mainly on changes to its survival MMO Dune: Awakening , with the Norwegian studio reworking the entire game to function as both a solo experience and a PvE adventure. Now that overhaul is done, however, Funcom is now set on expanding players' adventures on Arrakis, having just announced a free expansion that adds a new and completely different map to explore. Coming in December, the Blood and Ice DLC will let players depart the searing sands of Arrakis for the planet's frozen north, adding a new survival map called the Polar Sink that flips the game's central survival concept on its head. Rather than avoiding the heat, players will actively have to seek it out, while also developing new technologies to help them adapt to the extreme change in climate. There's some variance within this environment too. The Polar Sink is composed of two different biomes, the tundra and the icecap. While the icecap is the more extreme of the two, both areas are closely guarded by "water shippers", wealthy traders who supply Arrakis' second most-valuable resource from the polar regions down to the deserts. Players' primary objective in the DLC will be breaking the water shippers' stranglehold on the ice, which they can then use to cool their base equipment back in the desert and speed up resource production. Funcom says that the expansion adds "around 35 hours of new progression", which sounds pretty beefy for a free DLC. It also apparently "brings the focus back to ground-level survival" for veteran players, "traversal, temperature management and combat all playing important roles in your progression." Blood and Ice will be released on December 1. Alongside the expansion, Funcom has also introduced a Cosmetics Store to Awakening, and is also working on several other heavily requested features. These include an offline single-player mode that's coming in November (the game can be played solo right now, but only with an Internet connection) and fully supported cross-play in January next year. Funcom also says that Blood and Ice represents "another step in the ongoing development of Dune: Awakening" and that it will "continue expanding the game" through 2027. This falls in line with the studio's recent announcement that it was pivoting to exclusively support its existing games —which includes Conan Exiles alongside Dune: Awakening—and was laying off an unspecified number of employees as a result of that shift in strategy. 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. sources.text: Funcom's survival MMO Dune: Awakening is heading north with a free expansion that trades the deserts of Arrakis for a frozen new map. It's coming to PC, PS5, and Xbox. The new map, called the Polar Sink, turns the game's usual survival loop upside down. The map is split into two biomes, the tundra and the ice cap. You'll start in the tundra, where wealthy water shipper families have built lavish strongholds, before trying to get into the heavily guarded ice cap. Once you're in, you can harvest ice to cool your base equipment and speed up production. According to Funcom, the expansion "brings the focus back to ground-level survival, with traversal, temperature management, and combat all playing important roles in your progression". sources.title: Save Mass Effect Graffiti Reportedly Spray-Painted Outside EA Building
sources.text: An EA office building in Madrid was vandalized with the words "Save Mass Effect" just days after the company announced it had shuttered series developer BioWare. It's the latest update to an ongoing story that started when the beloved sci-fi RPG series was put on an indefinite hold earlier this month. With the studio's Mass Effect: Universe project canceled and the franchise without a future, fans have now seemingly taken their push to see the series continue with spray paint. EA's Madrid office in Spain was seemingly the target of one disgruntled fan hoping to make a change. Reddit user Ok_Link9625 shared pictures of the graffiti in question, which show at least two separate instances of Save Mass Effect being tagged around the location. "I stumbled upon the EA offices in Madrid as I was leaving a movie theater and saw this on the floor to the entrance and on the wall in front of the offices #SaveMassEffect," the post said. #SaveMassEffect is an idea that emerged in the moments after EA put the franchise on hold and laid off BioWare staff, but it didn't take long for it to become more than a social media hashtag. The days following the move saw fans erect a Save Mass Effect petition , which exploded and now stands at 290,000 signatures at the time of this piece's publication. As some fans called to boycott EA products over its decision, others, like the folks at We Are Mass Effect, took their love for the series to the streets of New York. It resulted in perhaps the most famous play for #SaveMassEffect thus far, as citizens in Times Square were treated to a billboard for the movement throughout October 26. The group said it plans to fund more billboards in the near future, including one set to go up outside this year's The Game Awards. I WENT OFFLINE FOR FEW HOURS AND SOMEONE PAINTED A WHOLE GRAFFITI IN FRONT OF EA OFFICE? Graffiti, however, is a new tactic, and it has received pushback in the community. While some want to keep the pressure up not only to breathe life into the franchise but also to support the people who have made it, others have said they aren't sure how tagging office buildings will move the needle. "I'll admit, I'm not sure this is the way to make them think the IP is worth saving," another top reply argued . Mass Effect series composer, meanwhile, simply took the opportunity to recognize how quickly the campaign has evolved in just a few days: "The fans are serious as a heart attack!" We absolutely did not ask people to do this and obviously vandalism is bad, but it's insane to me that #SaveMassEffect is so big that someone in Madrid is this angry. I get it. @heleuscluster Oh shi**, man, we have banksy on our side :D https://t.co/HNHAwdFAtL At the moment, it doesn't look like billboards or graffiti have done much to convince EA to support any angle the movement hopes to achieve. The most recent information about the fallout came from Bloomberg , which reported that the publisher canned its plans to release Mass Effect 5 in favor of prioritizing Star Wars Battlefront 3 . Alleged details about the canceled game promised that BioWare was creating a story that would have accounted for all choices players made in previous installments . sources.title: Input Lag Is So Bad in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 on Nintendo Switch 2 That Players Suffer From a 'Competitive Disadvantage'
sources.text: If you’re playing Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 on Nintendo Switch 2, beware: you’re at a disadvantage in competitive Multiplayer due to crushing input lag that is much worse than the other platforms. Digital Foundry’s analysis of the performance of the Switch 2 version of Modern Warfare 4 — the first Call of Duty released on a Nintendo console since 2013’s Ghosts — found that the input lag on Switch 2 can be two times longer than on PS5 at 60fps. In competitive Multiplayer, Switch 2 aims for 60fps and, according to DF, hits that target most of the time (although some things do cause the frame rate to drop, including looking through the transparent visor of a riot shield). Call of Duty Multiplayer prides itself on rock solid 60fps gameplay, which provides a smooth, responsive experience for those who fuss over their K/D ratio in, for example, 6v6. It’s crucial that all platforms the game is available on offer at least 60fps to provide a level playing field for Multiplayer fans — although the debate about the advantage PC players have over console has dogged Call of Duty since the dawn of crossplay. DF reports that Variable Refresh Rate (VRR) support “helps smooth out” framerate drops on supported displays, although you’ll have a harder time of it in terms of performance playing through portable mode. And then we come to responsiveness. DF’s tests show 81ms in docked mode and 100ms in portable mode, the latter of which is double the PS5’s 49.1. In fact, DF found that Multiplayer in portable mode ranged from 83ms at best to 125ms at worst. DF called this "actually deleterious to performance.” DF seems generally happy with the Switch 2 version, which was handled by port specialist Digital Legends with support from Infinity Ward. But if you’re into Multiplayer, the inescapable fact is you are at a disadvantage. No matter how fast your trigger finger, the Switch 2 will take longer to respond. Outside of Multiplayer it’s a different story. The Campaign runs at 30fps, which was good enough for IGN’s Simon Cardy when he played the Switch 2 version of Modern Warfare 4 . “Granted, the textures are nowhere near as detailed, with flat surfaces and faces smoothed over to give the impression of plasticine versions of the campaign’s characters,” he said. “It's by no means a looker, but considering the reduced horsepower Nintendo’s latest console is working with, the gameplay itself was smooth, running at 30fps at 4K while docked.” “Yes, it's quite a visual downgrade when compared to the likes of PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X, but that comes with the territory,” he continued. “And if you’re solely a Nintendo owner who’s been locked out of Call of Duty for over a decade, you’re getting a version of Modern Warfare 4 that feels every bit as snappy as the series usually is, even if it’s a bit muddier than Nintendo’s own crisp visuals.” Why is Call of Duty releasing on a Nintendo console now, 14 years after the last time? It has to do with Microsoft’s $69 billion acquisition of Activision Blizzard. Back when Microsoft was facing regulatory hurdles, one announcement designed to help convince the powers that be to green light the buyout was a 10-year commitment to bring Call of Duty to Nintendo following the merger. “Microsoft is committed to helping bring more games to more people — however they choose to play,” then Xbox boss Phil Spencer said in December 2022. Four years later, and with the Activision Blizzard buyout done and dusted, Call of Duty is on Switch 2. We’ve got an in-progress Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Walkthrough to help you through the campaign missions, plus All Collectible Note Locations , and all the Code Solutions you’ll need to open every keypad and container. For multiplayer, check out How to Level Up Fast in MW4 and our Essential Multiplayer Tips and Tricks alongside the Best MW4 Settings we recommend you use. DMZ is back, so we’ve got a handy DMZ Beginner’s Guide , too. Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. Crédito: Voxl O ano de 2026 está bastante movimentado no mercado de games, mas novembro promete ser um dos meses mais marcantes da história recente dos videogames. De um lado, temos Grand Theft Auto 6, um dos lançamentos mais aguardados de todos os tempos e que chega após anos de expectativa e adiamentos. Do outro, a Nintendo prepara o retorno de um dos maiores clássicos da indústria: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, em um remake que promete dividir os holofotes com a aventura da Rockstar. A proximidade entre os dois lançamentos já rendeu comparações com o fenômeno “Barbenheimer”, nome dado ao encontro inesperado entre Barbie e Oppenheimer nos cinemas, em julho de 2023. Na época, os filmes de propostas completamente diferentes transformaram a disputa nas bilheterias em um evento cultural, com espectadores abraçando a ideia de assistir às duas produções. Agora, a indústria dos games tem sua própria versão dessa disputa. Enquanto GTA 6 chega em 19 de novembro, o remake de Ocarina of Time está previsto para 5 de novembro, no começo do mês, colocando duas das franquias mais importantes dos videogames em rota de colisão. No entanto, essa “disputa” pode acabar sendo mais amigável do que o esperado por um motivo importante: o mercado é gigante e os títulos estreiam em plataformas bem diferentes. A comparação com o fenômeno Barbenheimer ganhou ainda mais força depois que o programa Saturday Night Live apresentou uma esquete sobre o confronto durante o quadro Weekend Update. Na brincadeira, os protagonistas dos dois jogos, Jason e Link, aparecem conversando com o apresentador Colin Jost sobre a expectativa em torno dos lançamentos de novembro. Interpretado por Marcello Hernández, Jason representa o lado caótico de GTA 6, descrevendo um dia que envolve fuga da prisão, assalto a banco, roubo de carros e até o sequestro de um Boeing Dreamliner. Já Link, interpretado por Mikey Day, apresenta uma rotina consideravelmente mais tranquila em Hyrule, envolvendo a compra de feijões mágicos e uma música tocada na ocarina. A diferença entre os personagens resume bem a proposta da comparação. Enquanto Jason encerra sua participação prometendo “destruição, caos e sexo”, Link oferece “quebra-cabeças e combate leve” como alternativa para os jogadores. A chegada de GTA 6 tem sido um dos principais fatores de influência no calendário de lançamentos de 2026. Diversas desenvolvedoras e distribuidoras evitaram colocar seus grandes jogos na mesma janela do título da Rockstar, temendo perder espaço e atenção do público para um lançamento que deve movimentar toda a indústria. O impacto já aparece no planejamento de outras empresas. Alguns jogos tiveram suas datas alteradas para fugir da concorrência, enquanto outros projetos foram empurrados para 2027. Afinal, GTA 6 não disputa apenas vendas: o jogo também deve dominar as conversas nas redes sociais, transmissões ao vivo, vídeos e a cobertura especializada durante semanas. A Nintendo, por outro lado, parece disposta a aproveitar a proximidade com uma estratégia diferente. Em vez de tentar competir diretamente com a Rockstar no mesmo dia, a empresa posicionou Ocarina of Time duas semanas antes do lançamento de GTA 6, apostando na força de uma franquia que atravessa gerações. Com isso, a empresa pode ganhar as atenções dos seus fãs e usuários fieis antes da estreia do aguardado game da Rockstar Games. Afinal, o Switch 2 já possui mais de 23 milhões de unidades vendidas e não receberá GTA 6, abrindo caminho para o sucesso de Zelda na plataforma. O peso de GTA 6 no mercado é difícil de ignorar. O novo capítulo da franquia é apontado por relatos da indústria como o videogame mais caro já produzido e promete levar os jogadores de volta a Vice City, agora integrada ao estado fictício de Leonida. A Rockstar também confirmou que o mapa será aproximadamente duas vezes maior que o de GTA 5, com um nível maior de detalhes. O lançamento também deve ser um acontecimento comercial fora do padrão. Executivos da indústria já projetam que parte dos jogadores poderá até tirar folga do trabalho para aproveitar a estreia, algo que ajuda a dimensionar a expectativa em torno do projeto. Lançado originalmente em 1998, o título marcou época ao estabelecer referências para aventuras em três dimensões e permanece entre as experiências mais celebradas da franquia The Legend of Zelda. sources.title: Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3: clássico da franquia completa 25 anos
sources.text: O jogo marcou um ponto de virada no que foi a primeira transição de plataforma da série. O retorno da trupe de skatistas contava com 13 profissionais, mas, infelizmente para nós brasileiros, Bob Burnquist ficou de fora pela primeira e única vez até Proving Ground. Isso aconteceu porque Bob havia fechado um contrato para aparecer em outro jogo, o ESPN X Games Skateboarding. A ausência do único latino abriu espaço para um dos nomes mais conhecidos dos anos 2000: Bam Margera. Publicado pela Activision (sob o selo Activision O2), o título chegou ao PlayStation, Nintendo 64, PC, Mac, Game Boy Color, Game Boy Advance, PlayStation 2, Xbox e GameCube. Boa parte desses lançamentos aconteceu ainda em 2001, mas algumas plataformas receberam o jogo apenas no ano seguinte. A desenvolvedora original, Neversoft, ficou responsável justamente pelas versões dos consoles mais modernas, deixando outras empresas como Shaba Games, Vicarious Visions e HotGen incumbidas das versões para PSX, GBA e GBC respectivamente. A versão do primeiro console da Sony foi portada pela Edge of Reality para o N64, já os ports feitos para PC e Mac (que foram baseados no game para PS2, Xbox e GC) foram de incumbência da Gearbox Software e da Beenox respectivamente. Outra curiosidade é que THPS3 foi oficialmente o último jogo lançado para o console de 64 bits da Nintendo (agosto de 2002), que havia sido descontinuado quatro meses antes. O game foi desenvolvido no motor gráfico RenderWare, criado em 1993 pela Criterion Games. No entanto, as versões do PlayStation e do Nintendo 64 rodavam na mesma engine de Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 2, a Apocalypse. Para se ter uma idéia, a RenderWare foi utilizada até a geração do PlayStation 4, e foi usada em clássicos como a trilogia 3D do GTA (III, Vice City e San Andreas). A Neversoft começou o terceiro milênio com os dois pés na porta ao tratar do novo Tony Hawk. Aproveitando as possibilidades das plataformas mais modernas, a empresa dedicou-se a criar muitas coisas novas para a franquia. A primeira delas, que mais marcou, foi o revert. A manobra permitia que os combos continuassem quando o skatista entrava em um quarter pipe (as manobras aéreas), apertando o botão quando encostasse na rampa ao cair e então emendar em um manual. Essa novidade foi tão importante que em jogos posteriores, como Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater HD, a DLC com mapas do terceiro jogo chamava-se Revert Pack. Até mesmo o primeiro remake recente, Tony Hawk’s 1+2, continha a manobra disponível, apesar de ela ainda não existir nos originais. Outra novidade que virou um marco da série foram os Hidden Combos. Basicamente eram variações de manobras feitas durante um manual, um flip ou um grind. Essas manobras foram inspiradas especialmente nas competições de freestyle, em que Rodney Mullen dava show no final da década de 1970 e nos anos 1980. Nessas competições, Mullen usava diversas variações do manual, indo para manobras como casper, anti-casper, handstand, entre outros; tudo isso sem perder o equilíbrio e sem “resetar” a sequência. No jogo, cada variação aumenta o multiplicador de pontos do combo nos casos de manual e grind. O flip trick apenas permitia uma nova manobra (como double kickflip) que valia mais pontos e gastava um tempo maior para ser realizada. Por falar nas manobras nos corrimãos, o balanço para grind e lip tricks foi adicionado ao game. Similar ao de manual, permitia um controle melhor e mais preciso para estender combos ao conseguir equilibrar o skatista. Essa foi outra ideia que permeou para sempre os jogos da franquia, uma vez que era mais complicado de manter o equilíbrio nos jogos anteriores (o personagem ia pendendo pra um lado somente, sem mais indícios). Algumas das ideias menores implementadas foram a inserção de pedestres e NPCs nos mapas, a possibilidade de criar uma skatista feminina (em THPS 2 só era possível criar atletas masculinos) e a remoção do Big Drop, permitindo quedas de alturas imensas sem perder o combo. Por fim, a principal novidade explorada pelo marketing do jogo foi o modo online. O que hoje é comum e avaliado como básico para qualquer título, naquela época a história era outra. Afinal, o PlayStation 2 não possuía modem embutido, o que já criava uma barreira. Além disso, era a época da conexão discada, a banda larga apenas começava a dar os primeiros passos no comércio para clientes finais nos grandes mercados. Antes do lançamento do adaptador de rede do console, era possível jogar online com adaptadores ethernet USB. A versão do Xbox, ironicamente, não possuía uma forma de jogar pela internet, apesar de o console contar com modem embutido. Apesar de ter contado com várias inovações, o núcleo principal do jogo permanecia o mesmo. Afinal, time que está ganhando não se mexe, e os jogos da série até então foram muito elogiados por todos. A gameplay básica permanecia a mesma para movimentação, para a execução das manobras, o funcionamento de gaps, enfim, esses aspectos foram apenas aprimorados. A proposta do game era a mesma: fases com dois minutos para realizar dez objetivos, que podiam ser feitos em várias tentativas, e outros níveis com o campeonato valendo a medalha de ouro, que consistia em três chances de um minuto cada para obter a maior nota. As fases eram liberadas conforme objetivos iam sendo realizados, ou conquistar uma medalha de bronze ao menos. Começava com Foundry, Canada, Rio de Janeiro (torneio), Suburbia, Airport, Skater Island (torneio), Los Angeles e Tokyo (torneio). As versões da sexta geração contavam ainda com Cruise Ship (também com dez objetivos) e mais versões remasterizadas da Warehouse, Burnside e Roswell. Os skatistas são basicamente os mesmos de THPS 2, exceto pela mudança mencionada anteriormente. A versão japonesa ainda recebeu quatro novos profissionais do país. sources.title: Tony Hawk Kicked Out Of Park While Trying To Recreate Pro Skater 3
sources.text: PlayStation 2 skateboarding Tony Hawk's Pro Skater Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3 + 4 Tony Hawk, skateboard legend, video game superstar and the last one to die in the great uprising , has inspired the culture for generations. Since Neversoft put him on the PlayStation in 1999, Hawk has been a household name, the video game series inspiring boarders on the couch and halfpipe alike. Looking to celebrate the 25th anniversary of Tony Hawkâs Pro Skater 3 , he traveled to the real world Los Angeles park recreated within the game. Only to be escorted out by security. “Happy 25th THPS3!” Posted the Birdman himself . “We got kicked out of Pershing Square while shooting this today.” Though unnamed in the game, the Los Angeles stage of Tony Hawkâs Pro Skater 3 is clearly inspired by Pershing Square, a business park in the cityâs financial district. With its distinctive modernist features from architect Ricardo Legorreta, the stone crescent benches and large red orbs made for a slick backdrop in the 2001 extreme sports game. It still remains in the city today, largely unchanged, as well as the nearby car wash with a big blue obelisk. As such, recreating the beloved video game should have made for easy content. To the Ramones’ Blitzkrieg Bop , Hawk rolls through Pershing Square, revisiting the sights, recreating the worbling idle stance of his virtual avatar. Leaving most of the tricks to his PlayStation self, Hawk and his team could only film so much before being ejected from the site by security. “She [security] just shooâd us away,” posted Hawk. “It was very anticlimactic.” The third entry in the series was the first to hit the PlayStation 2. To this day itâs considered not just one of the best in the series, but is tied with Grand Theft Auto 3 as Metacritic’s best on the console . The game was remade in 2025, part of Iron Galaxyâs Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3 + 4 bundle. While the first set was met with a ticker-tape parade, the secondâs reception was a touch milder . Fans young and old continue to be frustrated as getting new, no nonsense entries in any legacy skateboard series feels like pulling teeth, when they could be losing them off a botched rail grind instead. sources.text: F-Stop , Valveâs cancelled 2007 Portal prequel, has leaked onlineâand yes, itâs fully playable. If youâve heard of F-Stop , you donât need me to tell you why this is a huge deal. But if you havenât, then youâre in for quite the history lesson. In 2007, Valve spent three months on a project that Gabe Newell would later dub the Directed Design Experiments. Now, Iâm not going to attempt to tell the story better than the folks at the Half-Life wiki have before, so hereâs the short version: during these three months, Valve broke off into five teams. Each team designed and partially created a video game âexperiment,â and the fifth was dubbed â F-Stop .â F-Stop was conceptualised as a prequel to Portal , and the gameplay revolved around using an experimental Aperture Science camera to mess with perspectives and solve puzzles. Gabe Newell himself was very taken with the project, but playtesters were less thrilled. Ultimately, F-Stop was scrapped, and some of its dialogue, characters, and mechanics were reworked into Portal 2 . Well, consider it scrapped no longer, as thanks to the efforts of several leakers and the Valve Cut Content team , F-Stop is now playable in (almost) its entirety. If youâre curious as to how this leaked, the long answer is that itâs actually a combination of three separate leaks. Some of you might remember that in late August, roughly 13 terabytes of Steam depot data leaked online . The leak, dubbed Steam2, seemingly contained almost every Steam depot from 2003 to 2013 and, most surprisingly, assets for F-Stop . However, while the Steam2 leak included the majority of F-Stopâs assets, it did not include F-Stopâs source code or its mapsrc data (Valveâs folder name for its map source code data). It appears both of these final pieces of the F-Stop puzzle were leaked via the Valve Cut Content projectâs Discord server over the past 48 hours. According to the mods in the server, the person who leaked the F-Stop mapsrc initially asked for $1,000, but, for whatever reason, just ended up giving them away for free anyway. The Valve Cut Content team has verified the map files’ authenticity, and the community has combined all three of the puzzle pieces into the end result: a fully playable version of F-Stop . Those who have played it are reporting that while there appear to be a few missing assets and dialogue lines here and there, itâs essentially 99 percent complete. Unsurprising, as I’m sure Valve would have added a little more polish if they ever planned to release this officially, but hey, letâs be realââ99 percent completeâ is a hell of a lot more than the 0 percent complete we had this time last week. sources.title: Valve's long-lost prototype Portal prequel appears online after nearly 20 years
sources.text: F-Stop was a result of a post-Orange Box, 2007 Valve game jam. As reported by Kotaku , a near-mythical canceled Valve game called F-Stop has been reconstructed from material contained in separate leaks. Direct access to the build seems a little shaky at the moment, but full playthroughs of the game, like this one by Meme Man? on YouTube , are starting to pop up online. Most of F-Stop's assets came out in this August's Steam "teraleak," but the final pieces⁠—F-Stop's source code and mapsrc data⁠—were only just acquired by the Valve Cut Content Team Discord, which appears to have gone private amid all the newfound attention over F-Stop. With the Discord currently invite-only, you gotta know a guy (or know a guy who knows a guy) to play it yourself. The Half-Life Wiki has the skinny on F-Stop's origins in the "Directed Design Experiments." Following the megahit launch of the Orange Box in 2007, Gabe Newell effectively shut Valve down for a three-month game jam that produced five prototypes, F-Stop among them. It applied Team Fortress 2's cel-shaded art style to a vision of Aperture Science in its prime, all mid-century wood-paneled office optimism. F-Stop's central mechanic was a camera that could capture objects in the world, then place them elsewhere to solve puzzles. The excellent 2023 game Viewfinder would apply a similar concept to a full commercial release. But while loved internally at Valve, F-Stop's playtests were apparently more tepid. The game was shelved, though elements of its worldbuilding would appear in Portal 2 and Aperture Desk Job. It's fun to recognize some of these early ideas in the F-Stop longplays: From the jump, we get a version of Cave Johnson (sadly sans-J.K. Simmons in prototype) talking to the player, as well as the first instance of Aperture Personality Cores as companions in the puzzling. Given F-Stop's "road not taken" nature, particularly compared to the megathit Left 4 Dead and Portal 2 that would follow, I don't really mourn the fact that we never got to play its final version. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 teased a handful of its upcoming radio stations and its music curation is as strong as ever
sources.text: I can already picture my late-night Leonida drives to these bangers. Grand Theft Auto's radio stations have long stood as an integral part of the series' whole vibe—either offering time capsules of the times each game was set in (Vice City), or offering a realistic blend of classic and modernity a la Grand Theft Auto 5 's excellent music curation. Welcome to Critical Hit , where I (or someone else on the PC Gamer team) celebrate and lament all things videogame music, audio design, and the ways our favourite games make our ears tingle. I've been just a tad giddy to discover what awaits me in Grand Theft Auto 6 's car stereos when the game launches on November 19, which has me surprised that Rockstar teasing six of its upcoming stations earlier this month completely flew under my radar. Well, now I've had a gander and listened to all 12 minutes of its DJs bantering and a peppering of bangers between. And I gotta say, I'm already jazzed to speed down Leonida's highways with some of these stations at full volume. Rockstar's licensed music curation rarely misses, and that very much seems to be the continuing trend with Grand Theft Auto 6. While we don't know just how many radio stations there are in total yet—this is the first game where we'll be able to tune in to both terrestrial music stations and podcasts, it being 2026 and all—but the six that were teased were the exact kind of flavours I've come to expect from the series. There's Latin station Cocoteo FM, classic country Back Country Radio, African channel AfroBANK FM, all-out metal hub The Chamber 106.6, pop banger central Flash FM, and hip-hop destination Dirty South Classics. I'm already 100% here for The Chamber's setlist, being an elder emo and all, with bands like Black Sabbath, Pantera, and Slayer making their way onto Leonida's airwaves. But I'm also jazzed to see newer blood on the scene, like Bad Bunny's appearance on Cocoteo. My biggest interest was in Flash FM, though. Non-Stop Pop has become such an iconic radio station for me, thanks to some excellent song choices and Cara Delevigne's delightfully deadpan delivery. It doesn't seem like I'm going to be disappointed, though—Alex Consani takes up the mantle as model-turned-radio-host alongside the excellent artist Robyn (of Bulletproof fame), and hearing one of my favourite songs in MGMT's Electric Feel is all the confidence I need in Rockstar's keen ear. While the previews do show criminally little interactions between the hosts (it seems like Grand Theft Auto 6 is going for duos across all its stations, presumably for some easy back-and-forth banter), I'm sure there'll still be satire in droves to come. sources.text: Grand Theft Auto is arguably the most legendary and impactful video game franchise in history . It has been one of the most transformative titles ever concocted, changing the face of open-world games and presenting countless hours of exploration and entertainment opportunities to an audience numbering in the hundreds of millions over the years. But which Grand Theft Auto game is the best? It’s a tricky question, and as I write this, we’re staring down the barrel of Grand Theft Auto 6, which has the potential to be the biggest game of all time . Below, I’ve ranked all GTA games from worst to best, leaning on Metacritic for those handy scores while also leveraging my experience with the franchise. Let me know on the Insider Gaming Discord server if you agree with this ranking. Here’s the most comprehensive ranking of GTA games you’ll find anywhere (maybe). Remember, this is a combination of Metacritic scores and my personal opinion. Grand Theft Auto 2 is the lowest-rated GTA game ever made, according to Metacritic. It surfaced just around the turn of the millennium, emerging as the sequel to the controversial, scandalous game that changed everything forever. It wasn’t as well received, and, to be honest, I never really played it that much, even when I revisited the series as an adult. It’s a safe pick for the title of the worst GTA game ever made. It has the legacy vote and proved to be hugely transformative and shocking, but as a game , it received fairly mixed reviews. It was regarded as being pretty basic and poorly designed, and ultimately lacking substance. That meant that GTA wound up with a fair few low-tier review scores, as low as 6 out of 10 in some cases. It’s not the worst GTA game ever made, but it’s close. Vice City Stories was one of the spin-off titles that revisited an old location with a new playable character and a fresh story, and it was pretty well delivered. It landed first on PSP as a handheld-exclusive game, but was also ported to the PlayStation 2. Strangely, it managed to score a whopping 11 points more on PSP than on PS2, with more gamers appreciating the native handheld approach. This is one of the games that fans hope will be revisited in some way during Grand Theft Auto 6’s story, given that it takes place in a modern rendition of Vice City. The first spin-off title to make it to the PSP was Liberty City Stories, a stellar, standalone game that also wound up launching on PlayStation 2. Like Vice City Stories, it fared better in the review stakes on the handheld platform, but I really enjoyed it on my trusty PS2 console all those years ago. Some reviewers felt back then that it trumped GTA 3, which introduced the world of Liberty City, the obvious setting for this handheld title. Everything about Chinatown Wars felt unique at the time, from the art style to how it managed the open-world environment on low-end hardware. Amazingly, it featured the same base map as GTA 4, only a scaled-down version to account for it being a handheld game. It had a brilliant story and was a marvel for how ‘basic’ it was. Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas is a timeless classic that’s still immensely popular today. It took the 3D generation formula that had been delivered so well and blew it up, introducing the largest in-game map, multiple biomes, and a far-reaching and ambitious story that is still deeply memorable. For many, this is the best GTA game ever made, and it has been brought back to life numerous times over the years via remasters, ports, and mods. It still has a pretty decent RP community backing the multiplayer platform, too. Grand Theft Auto: Vice City was a game-changer in many ways. It might seem amazing, but it came out just one year after GTA 3 landed, and it introduced an entirely new setting, story, characters, and much more. That kind of delivery cadence is utterly unheard of today, but that’s the nature of the industry, I guess. GTA: Vice City is a beloved game with a lasting legacy, and it’s one that has heavily influenced the upcoming release of Grand Theft Auto 6. There are even throwback packs coming in GTA 6 that allow you to once again soak up the neon-drenched beauty of Vice City and get a taste of nostalgia. It became a product that many developers considered a bar, offering users an intense, gritty story and a marvellous world to explore. GTA 3’s influence can still be felt today, and the game’s setting, Liberty City, has become one of the most storied and revisited locales in GTA history, even if the base map hasn’t always stayed the same. It’s definitely a contender for the title of the best Grand Theft Auto game ever made, but it lands in third place in this ranking. sources.title: Hoyoverse’s Cozy Sim Petit Planet Coming to Nintendo Switch 2 in 2027
sources.text: Rejoice, Nintendo Switch 2 owners with a taste for the cozy, because Hoyoverse, the studio behind Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail, is bringing its new intergalactic life sim Petit Planet to Nintendo Switch 2 in 2027. The free-to-play game is already releasing on PC, iOS, and Android on December 4, 2026, but it never hurts to have more cute and cozy content on your Switch. The news came as part of a special update on the game from Hoyoverse, which also gave us a deep dive into some of the Petit Planet neighbors you can encounter, the home decor features, and some of the mini-games available as you live your life in Starsea. You start out taking care of your own planet, but can then explore the little islands in the skies around Starsea or visit the hub-style Galactic Bazaar for things like in-game auctions and community features. Petit Planet was announced back in September 2025, and IGN got to play it a few months later , with our writer describing it as Animal Crossing meets The Little Prince. "In my short time of about five hours with a preview of the closed beta, Petit Planet offered a charming, "The Little Prince"-themed take on Animal Crossing: New Horizons with an emphasis on clear progression and multiplayer. While these are two things some seemed to crave and were left empty in ACNH, the Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail studio may offer an answer – with potential caveats." The special update also revealed a bunch of chances for players to score pre-registration prizes as well as a "Launch a Planet" event on the game's official website that starts today. sources.title: Petit Planet coming to Switch 2 in 2027
sources.text: miHoYo will release a Switch 2 version of free-to-play cosmic life simulation game Petit Planet in 2027, the developer announced. It will launch first for PC via Epic Games Store and client download, iOS via App Store , and Android via Google Play on December 4, as previously announced . In Petit Planet , players take on the role of Planet Tenders, journeying to the Starsea on the back of Oumuamua, a Starsea Spirit said to listen to the wishes in people’s hearts. On their very own planet, they plant a Luca Seed that gradually grows into a Luca Arbor, shaping the planet’s landscape, seasons, and ecosystem over time. Life on the planet is never lonely. Planet Coordinator Mobai and Starsea Racer Elsasani are the first to welcome each Planet Tender to their new home, with more Neighbors arriving over time, each with their own stories to tell. As players get to know their Neighbors, chance encounters can blossom into lasting friendships. Beyond life on their home planet, players can set sail across the Starsea to explore its scattered Islets , or head to the Galactic Bazaar to enjoy games, take part in auctions, and share their creations. To celebrate the upcoming launch, HoYoverse has prepared a series of events and rewards for Planet Tenders. A pre-registration lucky draw on the official website offers exciting prizes, while over 1,000 clothing and furniture items can be earned for free through regular gameplay. In the “Besties, Made to Match!” event, players who team up with two friends to pre-register will each receive an exclusive clothing item. Starting November 1, the special “Launch a Planet” event invites players to design their own planets on the official event website, with a chance to win surprise grand prizes. The first Petit Planet Seasonal Creation Event will kick off alongside the game’s launch, offering cash prizes, in-game rewards, and official merchandise for selected fan creations. After the special program, players can also visit Petit Planet ‘s official X account to receive a “Moving Guide” and enter for a chance to win a suitcase, gift cards, and an exclusive luggage tag.
